title: Massachusetts Controlled Substances Registration and DEA registration by schedule
subtopic: Massachusetts and federal registration by schedule
rule_summary: The Department of Public Health's Massachusetts Controlled Substances Registration page states that Massachusetts General Laws, Chapter 94C, section 7 and regulations of the Department of Public Health at 105 CMR 700.004 require every person who manufactures, distributes, prescribes, administers, dispenses or possesses controlled substances in Schedules II-V to be registered with both the Department of Public Health (Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration (MCSR)) and the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). The page further states that Massachusetts law recognizes prescription drugs that are not federally scheduled (Schedule VI) as controlled substances; that practitioners who only plan to manufacture, distribute, dispense, prescribe, administer, or possess Schedule VI drugs only need to get an MCSR and not a DEA number; that both a DEA number and an MCSR are needed to conduct approved activities with controlled substances in Schedules II through V; and that the DEA and MCSR registrations must be for the same Schedules.
exam_relevance: Tests that Schedule II through V activity needs both registrations, held for the same schedules, and that activity limited to Schedule VI needs the Massachusetts registration without a DEA number.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Massachusetts Controlled Substances Registration
authority.section: Massachusetts Controlled Substances Registration page, statement of who must register with the Department and with the DEA

exceptions: A practitioner who only plans to manufacture, distribute, dispense, prescribe, administer or possess Schedule VI drugs needs an MCSR and not a DEA number.
common_confusions: Treating a DEA number as required for activity limited to Schedule VI.
Treating a DEA registration as sufficient for Schedule II through V activity without the MCSR.
Overlooking that the DEA and MCSR registrations must be for the same schedules.
verification_notes: Read on the Department of Public Health's Massachusetts Controlled Substances Registration page on mass.gov on 2026-09-14.
